name: Nimesulide
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) restricted in Europe because of serious liver injury. About half a dose is excreted in urine; in mild to moderate kidney impairment exposure rises about 50% without accumulation. The European harmonized text needs no change at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 30–80 mL/min and contraindicates it below 30 mL/min. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European harmonized summary of product characteristics (EMA 2004) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 100 mg twice daily after meals, for the shortest time possible (EMA 2004).
CrCl 30–80: no dose adjustment (EMA 2004). Caution: kidney function may deteriorate; stop if it does.

crrt: Contraindicated; NSAIDs worsen acute kidney injury.
monitoring: Liver function: stop permanently at any sign of liver injury or abnormal liver tests; avoid other hepatotoxic drugs and alcohol. Kidney function in CKD and heart failure; gastrointestinal bleeding (EMA 2004, 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Contraindicated under 12 years; adolescents 12 to 18 years as adults (EMA 2004).

renal.recommendation: Contraindicated under 12 years; adolescents follow adult kidney rules (contraindicated if CrCl <30).

sources.citation: European Medicines Agency. (2004). Nimesulide: Article 31 referral, Annex III (summary of product characteristics; CPMP/3086/03-REV.1).

adult: Source is the 2004 EMA harmonized SmPC. Later EMA reviews (2007, 2012) further restricted nimesulide (second-line use, maximum treatment duration); those documents were not retrieved, so the 15-day limit and second-line wording are NOT included. Retrieve the 2012 Annex before approval.
Nimesulide is banned or withdrawn in several countries for hepatotoxicity; consider a caution chip.
